propositions: Requiring canonical section headings (Approach, Scope) as hard rules rejects valid closed tickets whose plan content is carried by semantic aliases or non-heading compact format; section presence is coaching, not sound oracle.

Placeholder-phrase lexicon detectors (check if, TBD, TBC) cannot distinguish mechanically decidable bounded conditionals from deferred design; the signal is useful as advisory hint but disproven as hard failure criterion.

Explicit per-AC proof-coverage markers (verified by, verify with) are absent in valid closed tickets; behavioral assertions are self-contained oracles that do not require lexical proof-clause sentinels.
File-impact edit-set requirements must be exempt for read-only analysis, operational probes, and external-attestation work when an explicit no-edit output contract is present in the plan.

Deterministic AC conjunction-count heuristics cannot separate bundled independent deliverables from atomic cross-surface invariants; conjunction hygiene remains a review signal, not a validity oracle.

Testing section name-negative-scenario rules should not apply mechanically to non-user-facing mechanical work; applicability must be gated by semantic behavior classification, not heading presence alone.
